claims.text: On 11 August this was one website; by 26 August there were twenty repositories, nineteen of them siblings on *.sgit.ai, and fifteen of those were created in the last five days of that fortnight.
claims.quote: nineteen of them siblings on .sgit.ai, and fifteen of those were created in the last five days of that fortnight

value.unit: repositories, nineteen of them sibling sites

claims.text: The split was not a plan anybody wrote down; it is what happened when a body of work outgrew the shape it was being published in, and what matters is what the count did to the writing.
claims.quote: It is what happened when a body of work outgrew the shape it was being published in

claims.text: A section is a promise that something is part of the thing it sits inside; the promise held while the material was about sgit and stopped holding when the writing answered questions not about sgit at all.
claims.quote: A section is a promise that something is part of the thing it sits inside.

claims.text: The real forcing function was version history: nineteen arguments moving at different speeds through one release log produces a record nobody can read, and split, each argument gets its own tags, cadence and record of when it changed its mind.
claims.quote: Nineteen arguments moving at different speeds through one release log produces a record nobody can read.

claims.text: Discovery got worse before it got better: nineteen domains is not a menu, and a reader who does not already know the sites cannot pick one from a list of names.
claims.quote: Nineteen domains is not a menu, it is a problem.

claims.text: Consistency became something to maintain rather than get for free: one site has one stylesheet by construction, nineteen have one by discipline, and discipline is the thing that quietly stops happening.
claims.quote: Nineteen have one stylesheet by discipline, and discipline is the thing that quietly stops happening.

claims.text: Cross-linking stopped being automatic: a link between sites is a claim that the other site still says what you think it says, and graphs.sgit.ai is the only sibling so far that links back.
claims.quote: a link between sites is a claim that the other site still says what you think it says

claims.text: The audit that added the link back found the same site pointing at sentinel.sgit.ai, which does not exist; the site is sg-sentinel.sgit.ai, one character of drift and the link is dead.
claims.quote: One character of drift, and the link is dead.

claims.text: The directory used to be a list of cards and now starts from the question: signing off a risk points to risks.sgit.ai, calling an LLM without holding a key to llms.sgit.ai, an issue tracker with no database to issues-fs.sgit.ai.
claims.quote: So it now starts from the question, not the inventory

claims.text: The directory has seventeen question lines, then five groups by area, then a table of all nineteen: three ways in for someone with a problem, someone browsing a field, and someone auditing the whole set.
claims.quote: Seventeen lines like that, then five groups by area, then a table of all nineteen for anyone who would rather see everything at once.

claims.text: Every thesis on the directory page is the site's own words, quoted from its H1 or lede rather than summarised, because a summary drifts and a quotation either matches or is visibly wrong.
claims.quote: A summary drifts. A quotation either matches or is visibly wrong.

claims.text: None of this would be worth doing if each site were a bespoke build; they share the same generator, stylesheet, release script and validator, and the same rule that publishing is adding one file.
claims.quote: same generator, same stylesheet, same release script, same validator, same rule that publishing is adding one file

claims.text: Adding the twentieth site is writing one markdown file with a category and a one-line thesis; the property that makes nineteen sites tractable is the one that makes an unattended agent safe: two agents publishing the same day cannot conflict.
claims.quote: Adding the twentieth site to this index is writing one markdown file with a category and a one-line thesis.

claims.text: One of the nineteen is not published: skills.sgit.ai has a repository and a DNS record and nothing behind it, and is listed as not published yet rather than quietly omitted.
claims.quote: skills.sgit.ai has a repository and a DNS record and nothing behind it

claims.text: Most of the sites are arguments, not products: sg-sentinel.sgit.ai says NOT BUILT on every page, risks.sgit.ai states that zero lines of code implement its model, and wardley-maps.sgit.ai is marked PROPOSED.
claims.quote: Most of these sites are arguments, not products.

claims.text: That is the house style working as intended: publish the argument before the thing exists, say precisely what it is worth, and let it be checked later.
claims.quote: publish the argument before the thing exists, say precisely what it is worth, and let it be checked later
